title_en: Several Provisions of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on the Direct Election of Deputies to the People's Congresses at or below the County Level

articles.content_en: 1. Election committees shall be established in counties, autonomous counties, cities not divided into districts, municipal districts, townships, ethnic townships, and towns. The members of the election committee of a county, autonomous county, city not divided into districts, or municipal district shall be appointed by the standing committee of the people's congress at the corresponding level. The members of the election committee of a township, ethnic township, or town shall be appointed by the standing committee of the people's congress of the county, autonomous county, city not divided into districts, or municipal district. An election committee shall establish an operational office to handle specific election affairs.

2. The functions and powers of an election committee are as follows: (1) to preside over the election of deputies to the people's congress at the corresponding level; (2) to conduct voter registration, examine voters' qualifications, announce the list of voters, accept appeals concerning objections to the list of voters, and make decisions thereon; (3) to divide electoral districts for the election of deputies to the people's congress at the corresponding level and allocate the number of deputies to be elected in each electoral district; (4) to determine and announce the list of official candidates for deputies based on the opinions of the majority of voters; (5) to prescribe the date of election; and (6) to determine whether the election results are valid and announce the list of elected deputies. The election committee of a county, autonomous county, city not divided into districts, or municipal district shall supervise the work of the election committees of townships, ethnic townships, and towns.
3. A person with a mental disorder who is incapable of exercising the right to vote shall, upon confirmation by the election committee, not exercise the right to vote.

4. A person in custody who is undergoing investigation, prosecution, or adjudication for a counter-revolutionary case or other serious criminal case shall, by decision of the people's procuratorate or the people's court, cease to exercise the right to vote during the period of custody.

5. The following persons shall be permitted to exercise the right to vote: (1) those sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment, criminal detention, or public surveillance without the supplementary punishment of deprivation of political rights; (2) those in custody undergoing investigation, prosecution, or adjudication, and for whom the people's procuratorate or the people's court has not decided to cease the exercise of the right to vote; (3) those released on bail pending investigation or trial or under residential surveillance; (4) those undergoing re-education through labor; and (5) those subject to a penalty of detention. The participation of the above-listed persons in elections shall be jointly decided by the election committee and the organ executing imprisonment, custody, detention, or re-education through labor, and they may vote in a mobile ballot box or entrust a relative who has the right to vote or another voter to vote on their behalf. Persons sentenced to criminal detention, subject to a penalty of detention, or undergoing re-education through labor may also return to their original electoral district to vote on election day.

6. Where the seat of the people's government of a county or autonomous county is located within a city district, the employees of its subordinate organs, organizations, enterprises, and institutions shall participate in the election of deputies to the people's congress of the county or autonomous county and shall not participate in the election of deputies to the people's congress of the city or municipal district.

7. Employees of enterprises and institutions stationed in townships, ethnic townships, or towns that are not under the leadership of the people's government at or below the county level may participate only in the election of deputies to the people's congress at the county level and not in the election of deputies to the people's congress of the township, ethnic township, or town.
8. The size of an electoral district shall be divided based on the election of one to three deputies per electoral district.

9. Where a voter is temporarily working, employed, or residing in another place during the election period and cannot return to the original electoral district to participate in the election, with the approval of the election committee of the original place of residence, he or she may, in writing, entrust a relative who has the right to vote or another voter to vote on his or her behalf in the original electoral district. Where a voter has actually moved to another place but has not transferred his or her household registration, he or she may, after obtaining a certificate of voter qualification from the original electoral district, participate in the election in the electoral district of the current place of residence.

10. The number of candidates for deputies nominated by each voter (with the endorsement of three or more persons) shall not exceed the number of deputies to be elected in that electoral district. All candidates for deputies nominated by voters, political parties, and people's organizations shall be included in the list of candidates for deputies, and the election committee shall not substitute, add, or delete any of them. The list of official candidates for deputies, if determined through a preliminary election, shall be arranged in descending order of the number of votes received.
